entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd al-Raḥmān al-Sakhāwī was a Shafi‘i Muslim hadith scholar and historian who was born in Cairo. Al-Sakhawi refers to the village of Sakha in Egypt, where his relatives belonged. He was a prolific writer that excelled in the knowledge of hadith, tafsir, literature, and history. His work was also anthropological. For example, in Egypt he recorded the marital history of 500 women, the largest sample on marriage in the Middle Ages, and found that at least a third of all women in the Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt and the Bilad al-Sham married more than once, with many marrying three or more times.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Al-Sakhawi's work on hadith and history provides a unique window into the social dynamics of medieval Egypt, including the marital habits of women in the Mamluk Sultanate. His research has been cited by later historians and continues to inform our understanding of Islamic society during this period.
